checkpoints: A fixed TTL with no jitter means every concurrent reader of the same hot key shares an identical expiry moment, so the instant that boundary passes, all of them see a cache MISS at the same instant rather than staggered over time.

This synchronized MISS is a cache stampede (thundering herd): each of the ~50k concurrent readers independently falls through the edge cache straight to the shielded origin at the same instant, instead of one request rebuilding the entry on behalf of the rest.

`proxy_cache_valid 200 60s` only governs when a cached entry goes stale — it says nothing about how many concurrent requests are allowed to react to that staleness by hitting the origin, so origin CPU/DB load spikes periodically in lockstep with the TTL rather than staying steady.

Request coalescing via `proxy_cache_lock on;` fixes the root cause by letting exactly one of the concurrent MISSes actually reach `/api/cdn/origin/:fileId/:chunkIndex` to rebuild the entry, while every other concurrent request for that same cache key waits on that single in-flight rebuild instead of independently calling the origin.

Pairing coalescing with `proxy_cache_use_stale updating;` lets the edge keep answering the other waiting requests with the still-cached, slightly stale chunk during the rebuild window, so those clients get an immediate 200 instead of blocking behind the lock until the single rebuild finishes.

The staleness this introduces is bounded to roughly one origin round trip — the time the single coalesced rebuild takes (the 150ms `readChunk` cost) — which is a deliberate, acceptable trade-off in exchange for turning tens of thousands of simultaneous origin hits into one.

Because the origin sets an `ETag` from the chunk's SHA256, the single coalesced rebuild request can revalidate as a cheap `304 Not Modified` instead of re-sending the full chunk body, making the one allowed-through request even cheaper than a full refetch.

The fix can be verified by driving concurrent load against the same fileId/chunkIndex exactly across a 60s expiry boundary: before the fix the origin sees a burst of roughly 50k hits at each expiry, and after adding `proxy_cache_lock` plus `proxy_cache_use_stale updating;` the origin sees roughly one request per key per refill cycle while `X-Cache` still shows a clean MISS-then-HIT/stale pattern with no error responses.
